messages:
anika: heads-up — hit a perf regression in paged-attn under bursty traffic, seems tied to block-table fragmentation. latency p95 up ~30% when KV pages are being split/merged. anyone seen similar?

matt: can you repro locally with a synthetic workload? numbers + perf profile would help.

anika: repro is deterministic on my desktop. workload: 64 concurrent streams, avg seq 1024, 1:4 mix short/long. run:
```bash
./bench_paged_attn --concurrency 64 --seq-dist=long-heavy --kv-page-size=4k
```
p95 190ms -> baseline 145ms. attaching perf flame (s3://redwood-dev/tmp/paged-flame-177345).

samir: ugh fragmentation. is the allocator doing first-fit on block-table? if we keep many half-empty blocks, coalescing only happens at eviction which is too late.

anika: yeah current allocator: first-fit on free-list per-sizeclass, coalescing on free only if adjacent block present. we frequently split blocks for small KV pages and never rejoin because eviction order scatters free pieces.

leo: two quick ideas: 1) opportunistic defrag during low-util windows (background merge), 2) prefer large contiguous allocations for new long requests to reduce splits. both cheap to try. :thumbsup:

matt: also check kernel selection — fused-attn kernels assume contiguous key/value layout; paged layout causes extra copy overhead. profile shows memcpy hotspots right after attention kernel.

anika: confirmed — flame shows memcpy spikes between attention and sharded-kernel call. when pages are non-contiguous we do an extra gather into a staging buffer.

samir: simple allocator patch: bump-scan coalesce pass that merges adjacent free pieces up to N bytes per cycle. pseudo: 
```cpp
void background_defrag() {
  for (auto slab : slabs) {
    scan_free_list(slab, budget_bytes=1<<20);
    merge_adjacent();
  }
}
```
should limit CPU impact.

leo: I'd prefer a policy change first: for long-context requests, attempt to reserve a contiguous chunk by scanning for a slab with enough contiguous space before splitting. fallback to split if not found. cheap and model-aware.

anika: can implement both: latency-critical path prefer-contig, and separate background defrag sweep. i'll prototype.

matt: add a metric for "blocks_splits_per_minute" and "contig_alloc_hit_rate" so we can AB test. also add an experiment flag.

anika: will do. one more wrinkle: dedicated capacity customers saw less regression — their KV page churn is lower due to sticky routing. suggests churn + small-capacity slabs amplify fragmentation.

samir: yep that explains it. maybe adapt slab size by tenant churn profile. high-churn tenants get larger page-size or different slab binning.

infra-bot: CI build #4821 finished — tests: paged-attn-allocation (flaky) failed on linux-amd64.

matt: good catch, maybe our unit tests need to simulate churn patterns. add a stress test that randomly interleaves short/long requests with eviction enabled.

anika: filing a follow-up PR with: contig-first allocation, bg defrag, two metrics, and stress test. putting draft up at: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1293

leo: great. assign me for review when ready. I'll also add a quick perf harness to capture memcpy counts.

samir: if you want I can prototype adaptive slab binning (per-tenant) — low effort.

anika: thanks all — will iterate tomorrow. :wave:
